//: TRI-RUNTIME BEHAVIOURAL FIXTURE for the maneuver-planner command surface. Every case here is byte-diffed across the browser harness, native WasmEdge and the pinned Docker WasmEdge, at 1/2/4/8 threads. Success paths AND failure paths: a deterministic error is parity evidence exactly like a deterministic answer, and this module's failure path is a TRAP (its exceptions are compiled out), so the trap CLASS is what must match rather than an error payload. Run: space-data-module parity --wasm dist/isomorphic/module.wasm --fixture parity/maneuver-command.json --lanes browser,wasmedge,docker-wasmedge
name: maneuver-command-parity

cases.//: The canonical case the program pins. Also the tightest possible parity probe: a closed-form answer that is a handful of sqrt() calls, so any divergence between lanes is a libm difference and nothing else.

Positive phase angle: the phasing orbit is SMALLER and the first burn is retrograde. The response carries only the magnitude, so what this case pins across lanes is that phasingSMA — the quantity the console wrapper recovers the sign from — is byte-identical everywhere.

170 degrees in one revolution: the module returns a phasing orbit whose far apse is roughly 4300 km BENEATH the surface, with no error and no flag. It is in the parity fixture deliberately — the defect must be reproduced IDENTICALLY on all three runtimes, so that the console-side Earth-collision guard is known to be guarding the same behaviour everywhere and not papering over a lane-specific quirk.

Tudat's elliptical Lambert case — the one geometry the solver gets right (it reaches the target to 5.8e-11 of |r2|). Included so that when the Lambert defect is repaired, the parity lane is already watching this operation on all three runtimes.

The module's exceptions are compiled out, so an unknown operation aborts instead of returning make_error_result. The trap CLASS must be the same on every runtime — a module that traps in the browser and returns an error under WasmEdge is not isomorphic, whichever behaviour is the desirable one.
numRevs = 0 hits the module's OWN validator, which throws a carefully worded message that no caller can ever observe. Pinned so the day it becomes reachable is a visible change in this lane.

cases.stdinUtf8: this is not a PIV invoke frame
cases.//: Below the JSON bridge entirely: the host codec's own rejection path, which must also agree across lanes.
